data.name: Meta_LanguageName
data.comment: This language's name in itself, shown in the Options dropdown. A language picker names each language the way its own speakers write it, so this is the one key a translator writes in their own language rather than translating: Deutsch, not German.

data.name: Meta_TranslationCredit
data.comment: Who translated this language, shown under the Options language dropdown - "Deutsch von Alex Weber", written in the translated language rather than in English. Left empty here because the app's own text is not a translation of anything; the line is hidden whenever this is empty, so a language whose translator would rather not be named simply leaves it alone.

data.name: Meta_ShippedLanguages
data.value: en, de, fr, it, ru, qps-ploc
data.comment: Every language tag this build ships, comma separated, English first. Adding a language means dropping in Strings.<tag>.resx and adding its tag here - the whole of it. Read from this file only, never from a translation, so translating this key cannot change what the app offers. A tag with no resources behind it is dropped at startup, which is how qps-ploc can sit here permanently and still only appear in a build made with -p:PseudoLocale=true.

data.name: Options_Language_Description
data.value: The language this app's own text is read in. System default follows the display language Windows is set to. Mod names, descriptions and changelogs come from the Forge and stay in whatever language their author wrote them in.

data.name: Options_Language_SystemDefaultFormat
data.comment: {0} is the language following Windows currently lands on, named in itself - "System default (English)".

data.name: Common_ClearFilters
data.comment: Button label, on both Browse and Installed. Each page explains its own in a tooltip.

data.name: Common_SaveAsDefault
data.comment: Button label, on both Browse and Installed.

data.name: Common_Previous
data.comment: Pager button, on both Browse and Installed. The previous page of results.

data.name: Common_Next
data.comment: Pager button, on both Browse and Installed.

data.name: Common_PinnedToolTip
data.value: Pinned - applying a collection never disables this mod
data.comment: On the pin icon. Five copies: Browse, Installed's three views, and a Mod lists entry.

data.name: Common_DownloadsFormat
data.comment: {0} is a download count. Keep the :N0 - it is what groups the thousands the way the user's Windows regional setting does.

data.name: Common_Close
data.comment: Tooltip on the mod details dialog's close button.

data.name: Common_Unknown
data.comment: Stands in for a version that could not be determined. Appears mid-sentence in Installed_DetailInstalledVersionFormat, so it is lower case in English.

data.name: Common_Rescan
data.comment: Button label - reads the install folder again.

data.name: Common_SearchPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the search box. "@author" is typed syntax, not a word - leave it as it is and translate only the sentence around it.

data.name: Common_ClearFiltersToolTip
data.value: Puts every filter back to what this page opens with.

data.name: Common_AttributeFilterToolTip
data.value: Filter by Fika support, ads, dependencies and addons
data.comment: Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Common_PageSizeToolTip

data.name: Common_PagerFormat

data.name: Dependencies_Refresh
data.comment: Button label - re-runs the dependency scan.

data.name: Addons_Description

data.name: Addons_OpenPage
data.value: Open this addon's page on sp-mod.com
data.comment: sp-mod.com is a domain and stays as it is.

data.name: Addons_InstalledFormat
data.comment: {0} is a version number.

data.name: Dependencies_Description
data.value: Mods installed twice or shipping clashing files, then every installed mod that declares dependencies and whether each one is satisfied. Problems are listed first.

data.name: Browse_SaveAsDefaultToolTip
data.value: Opens this page with the filters and sort it is set to right now, including the SPT version ticks. The search box is not included, and Per page needs no saving - the page keeps the one last picked. Options can clear it again.

data.name: Browse_RefreshCache
data.comment: Button label - re-fetches the mod catalog from sp-mod.com.

data.name: Browse_SptVersionFilterToolTip
data.value: Filter by the SPT releases a mod supports

data.name: Browse_SptVersionItemFormat
data.comment: One tick box in the SPT version filter. {0} is a version number; SPT is a product name.

data.name: Browse_CategoryFilterToolTip
data.value: Filter by the category a mod is listed under

data.name: Browse_FeaturedFilterToolTip
data.value: Whether mods featured on sp-mod.com are included

data.name: Browse_ByAuthorFormat
data.comment: {0} is an author's name, shown under a mod's title on its card.

data.name: Common_FlagFikaCompatible
data.comment: Badge on a mod card and one flag on an installed card's summary line. Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Common_FlagContainsAds
data.comment: Badge on a mod card and one flag on an installed or addon card's summary line.

data.name: Browse_BadgeHasDependencies
data.comment: Badge on a mod card.

data.name: Browse_AddonBadgeToolTip
data.value: Open this mod to see and install its addons

data.name: Browse_StartupProgressFormat
data.comment: First-run progress while the catalog downloads. {0} is how many have arrived, {1} the total.

data.name: Browse_FirstLaunchNote
data.value: The first launch downloads the mod catalog. After that it's read from disk and this is over in a moment.

data.name: Installed_ExpandAllToolTip
data.value: Open every mod the filters match

data.name: Installed_CollapseAllToolTip
data.value: Close every mod the filters match

data.name: Installed_ViewCards
data.comment: One of the three view buttons. A grid of cards.

data.name: Installed_ViewGroups
data.comment: One of the three view buttons. Mods sorted into the user's own groups.

data.name: Installed_ViewGroupsToolTip
data.value: Sort mods into your own groups, MO2-separator style.
data.comment: MO2 is Mod Organizer 2, another modding tool - a name, not a word.

data.name: Installed_ViewList

data.name: Installed_ViewListToolTip
data.value: One scrollable row per mod, each opening onto its full details.

data.name: Installed_ListBadges
data.comment: Label on the switch that shows mod-list chips on each mod. "List" here means a mod list, not the List view.

data.name: Installed_ListBadgesToolTip
data.value: Show which mod lists each mod belongs to.

data.name: Installed_UpdateFilterToolTip
data.value: Filter by whether an update is available

data.name: Installed_EnabledFilterToolTip
data.value: Filter by whether a mod is enabled or disabled

data.name: Installed_CategoryFilterToolTip

data.name: Installed_GroupFilterToolTip

data.name: Installed_SelectionClear

data.name: Installed_SelectAllToolTip

data.name: Installed_UpdateSelectedToolTip
data.value: Queue an update for every selected mod that has one. Mods with no update, disabled mods and addons are skipped.

data.name: Installed_SortGroupsLabel
data.comment: Label to the left of the group sort dropdown.

data.name: Installed_NewGroupPlaceholder

data.name: Installed_ListChipToolTip

data.comment: On each mod-list chip. The chip itself carries a list name the user typed, which is not translated.

data.name: Installed_DetailInstalledAsFormat
data.comment: {0} is the folder name on disk, shown when it differs from the mod's name.

data.name: Installed_DetailGuidFormat

data.name: Installed_DetailInstalledVersionFormat

data.name: Installed_DetailInstalledOnFormat

data.comment: Button that opens the mod's BepInEx folder in Explorer.

data.name: Installed_ServerFolder

data.name: Installed_DetailsAndVersionsToolTip

data.value: This mod is in both an enabled and a disabled folder - pick which copy to keep

data.name: Installed_RemoveToolTip

data.name: Installed_DisabledTag

data.name: Installed_GroupRowToolTip

data.name: ModLists_CaptureDescription
data.value: Records the mods that are currently enabled, at the versions you have.

data.name: ModLists_NamePlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the box for naming a new list.

data.name: ModLists_Capture
data.comment: Button label - makes a list out of what is installed now.

data.name: ModLists_ImportToolTip
data.value: Open a mod list someone shared with you

data.name: ModLists_SavedEmpty
data.value: Nothing saved yet. Capture what you have installed, or import a list someone sent you.

data.name: ModLists_ServingBadge
data.comment: Badge on the list this machine serves to clients. Short: it sits in a small chip.

data.name: ModLists_ServingToolTip
data.value: This machine serves this list to clients that connect to it. Editing and saving it republishes what they see.

data.name: ModLists_FromServerBadge
data.comment: Badge on a list a server handed to this install.

data.name: ModLists_FromServerToolTip
data.value: A server handed this list to you. It stays exactly as that server wrote it - make a copy to change what's on it.

data.name: ModLists_FollowingServerToolTip
data.value: This install is following this server's list, alongside its own

data.name: ModLists_FollowingToolTip
data.value: This install is following this list

data.name: ModLists_UndoToolTip
data.value: Puts every mod back the way it was before that list was applied. Usually just moves mods - nothing to download.

data.name: ModLists_PreviewToolTip
data.value: Work out what applying this list would do. Nothing moves and nothing downloads.

data.name: ModLists_ApplyToolTip
data.value: Download what's missing, enable what the list names, and set aside what it doesn't.

data.name: ModLists_BackToModsToolTip
data.value: Stop showing the plan and go back to what this list names. Changes nothing.

data.name: ModLists_ExportToolTip
data.value: Save this list to a file you can send to someone. It carries which mods and versions - never the mod files themselves.

data.name: ModLists_RefreshFromServerToolTip
data.value: Asks the server for this list again, even if its revision hasn't moved - which is what an operator editing and republishing the list they serve looks like from here. Nothing is installed or enabled; applying it is still a separate step.

data.name: ModLists_MakeCopyToolTip
data.value: Imported lists are read-only. This starts your own copy of it.

data.name: ModLists_StopFollowingToolTip
data.value: Clears which list this install is following. Nothing on disk changes.

data.name: ModLists_DeleteToolTip
data.value: Removes the list. Nothing on disk changes.

data.name: ModLists_AddModsToolTip
data.value: Put mods on this list - ones you have installed, or ones from sp-mod.com you haven't. Nothing is downloaded.

data.name: ModLists_RefreshVersionsToolTip
data.value: Reads the version of every mod on this list that is installed here, and updates the list to match. Scope is left alone, and mods you don't have are left as written. Nothing is downloaded or installed - Save keeps the changes.

data.name: ModLists_SaveToolTip
data.value: Write these changes to the list. Nothing is installed, enabled or disabled - Apply does that.

data.name: ModLists_DiscardToolTip
data.value: Throw these changes away and show the list as it is saved.

data.name: ModLists_PublishToolTip
data.value: Writes this list into the Server Map mod's config folder on this machine, so the server serves it to connected clients. Nothing is installed or changed on disk.

data.name: ModLists_ImportedNotice
data.value: This list came from someone else, so it stays exactly as they wrote it. Make a copy to change what's on it.

data.name: ModLists_EntrySearchToolTip
data.value: Matches the mod's name, the name the list stored, and the folders it installs into.

data.name: ModLists_ScopeFilterToolTip
data.value: Show only the entries meant for one kind of machine. Server only are the mods a player is never asked to install; Client only are the ones a Fika headless client skips.

data.name: ModLists_EntrySortToolTip
data.value: Ordered by the name shown on the row.

data.name: ModLists_NoEntries
data.value: This list names no mods yet. Add some, or capture what you have installed as a new list.

data.name: ModLists_NoMatches
data.value: Nothing on this list matches. Everything is still here - widen the search or the scope filter to see it.

data.name: ModLists_ScopeToolTip
data.value: Which machines this entry is for - the server, playing clients, a Fika headless client, or any combination of them. Capture works this out from where the mod's files live; change it for the exceptions, like a server mod nobody playing needs to install, or a HUD mod a headless client has no use for.

data.name: ModLists_RemoveEntryToolTip
data.value: Take this mod off the list. It stays installed - nothing on disk changes.

data.name: ModLists_PinToolTip
data.value: Pin this mod so no list you apply ever sets it aside. For the HUD and quality-of-life mods you want kept whatever list you switch to. Unpin it here or from the mod in Subscribed items.

data.name: ModLists_UnpinToolTip
data.value: Unpin this mod. Lists will be able to set it aside again, and this one would.

data.name: Options_InstallFolderDescription
data.value: Point this at your SPT game folder - the one with EscapeFromTarkov.exe in it, not the SPT server folder inside it. Once set, the installed SPT version is used to default the Browse version filter and to flag mods that aren't built for it.
data.comment: SPT.Server.exe is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_MachineRoleDescription
data.value: A Fika headless client hosts raids without anybody playing on it, so it needs the mods that decide how a raid goes - bots, items, locations - and none of the ones that draw things at a player. Saying which this machine is lets a mod list a server hands you arrive trimmed to what this machine actually needs. It never changes a list of your own, and it never affects what you can install by hand.
data.comment: Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_PlaysHereToolTip
data.value: Turn this off for a dedicated headless box - one that hosts raids and that nobody sits at.

data.name: Options_PlaysHereOn
data.comment: Label on a switch, shown when it is on.

data.name: Options_PlaysHereOff
data.comment: Label on the same switch, shown when it is off.

data.name: Options_HeadlessToolTip
data.value: Detected from the Fika headless launcher in the install folder, and overridable here for a setup that starts its headless some other way.

data.name: Options_HeadlessOn
data.value: This machine runs a Fika headless client

data.name: Options_HeadlessOff
data.value: This machine does not run a headless client

data.name: Options_NoHeadlessLauncherNotice
data.value: No Fika headless launcher was found in the install folder, so nothing here starts one - name it below, or leave it and the switch above still decides which mods a served list brings.

data.name: Options_HeadlessLauncherDescription
data.value: Leave this empty and the app looks for FikaHeadlessManager.exe at the top of the install folder. Point it at the exe yourself if it lives anywhere else - it does not have to be inside the install folder at all. It is used as-is, and ignored if the file isn't there.
data.comment: FikaHeadlessManager.exe is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_HeadlessLauncherPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the launcher path box - it means the app will look for it.

data.name: Options_ClearHeadlessLauncherToolTip
data.value: Back to looking in the install folder.

data.name: Options_AppearanceDescription
data.value: Follow system matches Windows and keeps matching it when you change it there. Light and Dark pin the app to one regardless.
data.comment: Follow system, Light and Dark are the three entries of the dropdown below - translate them the same way there.

data.name: Options_WindowDescription
data.value: How the window opens. Remembering the last size and position is the default, since dragging the window to a size and leaving it there is already an answer. Full screen fills the whole monitor with no title bar and covers the taskbar, which maximised does not - F11 switches into and out of it at any time, whichever of these is chosen.
data.comment: F11 is a keyboard key and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_WidthPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the window width box.

data.name: Options_HeightPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the window height box.

data.name: Options_UseCurrentSizeToolTip
data.value: Fills these boxes from the window as it is right now. Restore it down from maximised first - a maximised window has no chosen size to read.

data.name: Options_PageDefaultsDescription
data.value: Browse has a Save as default button under the gear beside its search box: it opens Browse with the filters and sort it is set to at the time. Subscribed items needs no button - it opens with the filters, sort and view you last left it on, and Clear filters there puts them back to the app's own. What you have typed in a search box is never kept. Per page needs no saving either: every page opens on Infinite until you pick a size there, then keeps the one you last picked.
data.comment: Save as default and Clear filters are the two buttons named in Common_SaveAsDefault and Common_ClearFilters - translate them the same way here.

data.name: Options_ClearBrowseDefault
data.comment: Browse is the page name, as in the sidebar.

data.name: Options_ModPagesDescription
data.value: Before anything downloads, this app asks you to open the mod's page - where its author puts install steps, requirements, known conflicts and warnings. Turn that off if you would rather go straight to installing. This app's own updates always ask, since that page is where its release notes are.

data.name: Options_FootprintDescription
data.value: Adds a page that reads the files each installed mod ships and describes how much of the game it is positioned to touch, and where any cost would land - client or server, CPU, GPU, memory or start-up. Nothing on it is timed or measured: what a mod actually costs you depends on your hardware, your settings and the other mods you run, none of which it can see. A heavy footprint means a mod reaches a long way into the game, which is usually why you installed it - it is a place to start looking, not a verdict. Off by default.

data.name: Options_ServerMapDescription
data.value: Adds a page that connects to an SPT server running the Server Map mod, so you can see what it runs and compare it against what you have installed. The mod goes on the server, not here - without it this page has nothing to show, which is why it is off by default. Use the same address and port you put in the SPT launcher; connecting sends nothing about your install, it only asks the server who it is.
data.comment: Server Map is the mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_ServerMapModNotice
data.value: Running a server? The Server Map mod is a separate download - get it from the mod's page and install it on the machine running SPT. Players joining that server need nothing but this switch.

data.name: Options_GetServerMapModToolTip
data.value: Opens the Server Map mod's page on sp-mod.com in your browser.

data.name: Options_ServerAddressPlaceholder
data.comment: 127.0.0.1 is an address and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_SharedKeyPlaceholder
data.value: Shared key (if the server needs one)

data.name: Options_GenerateKeyToolTip
data.value: Replaces this server's key with a new one. Everyone using the old key stops being able to see what this server publishes until you send them the new one. The server picks it up without being restarted.

data.name: Options_ForgetCertificateToolTip
data.value: Clears the recorded fingerprint. The next connection records whatever the server presents, the same as the first one did.

data.name: Options_DataFilesDescription
data.value: View or hand-edit the JSON files this app keeps under Data\, including installed-mods.json - useful when Subscribed items' own version controls aren't enough.
data.comment: Data\ and installed-mods.json are a folder and a file name - leave both exactly as they are.

data.name: Common_Cancel
data.comment: Dismisses a confirmation on the Play page, and cancels a download on the Downloads page.

data.name: ModUpdate_CurrentlyInstalledFormat
data.comment: {0} is a version number, or the Common_Unknown word when the app cannot tell.

data.name: ModUpdate_DowngradeToolTip
data.value: Install this older version in place of the one you have. Asks first - an older build may not read config or profile data the newer one wrote.

data.name: ModUpdate_MarkUpToDateToolTip
data.value: Record the newest published version as installed, without downloading anything

data.name: ModUpdate_ConfirmAsInstalledToolTip
data.value: Record the version selected below as installed, without downloading anything

data.name: ModUpdate_ClearOverrideToolTip
data.value: Go back to auto-detecting this mod's version from the files on disk

data.name: ModUpdate_Set
data.comment: Button beside the manual version box - records what was typed.

data.name: ModUpdate_ManualVersionPlaceholder
data.comment: 1.4.2 is an example version number.

data.name: ModUpdate_ShowAllToolTip
data.value: Include versions built for other SPT releases. They are hidden by default because you cannot use them on the SPT version you have.

data.name: ModUpdate_PublishedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a date, or the Common_Unknown word. Keep the :d - it prints the date the way the user's regional setting does.

data.name: ModUpdate_BadgeLatest
data.comment: Badge on the newest published version. Short: it sits in a small chip.

data.name: ModUpdate_BadgeInstalled
data.comment: Badge on the version currently on disk.

data.name: ModUpdate_TargetsSptFormat
data.comment: {0} is an SPT version or range, e.g. "3.10.x".

data.name: Play_ServerDescription
data.value: Starts this install's server and leaves it running in its own console window. It keeps running if you close this app. While it runs, Start server becomes Stop server. Restart stops it and starts it again - for a config edited or a server mod dropped in.
data.comment: Restart is the button named in Play_Restart - translate it the same way.

data.name: Play_Restart
data.comment: One button label used twice on this page: restarting the server, and restarting the headless launcher.

data.name: Play_RestartServerToolTip
data.value: Stops this install's server and starts it again. Only this install's - a second SPT server on another folder is left alone.

data.name: Play_RestartServerWarning
data.value: Restarting the server ends any raid running on it. Anyone in one is dropped.

data.name: Play_RestartServerConfirm
data.comment: Confirms the warning above it.

data.name: Play_LauncherDescription
data.value: Opens SPT.Launcher.exe, where you pick a profile and start the game. Start the server first - the launcher has nothing to log in to without it.
data.comment: SPT.Launcher.exe is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: Play_HeadlessHeader
data.comment: Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Play_HeadlessDescription
data.value: This install has a Fika headless launcher, which only appears on a setup running a headless client. It hosts raids for other players rather than being the one you play on - start the server first, same as the game launcher.

data.name: Play_RestartHeadlessToolTip
data.value: Stops the headless launcher and starts it again. It does not touch the server, and it does not close a game the launcher had already started.

data.name: Play_RestartHeadlessWarning
data.value: Restarting the headless ends any raid it is hosting. The server is left running, and a game this launcher already started is left alone - close that yourself if it needs to go too.

data.name: Configs_NoMatches
data.value: Nothing matches. Note that plenty of plugins only write a config the first time the game runs.

data.name: Configs_EmptyState
data.value: Pick a config file on the left to edit it.

data.name: Configs_ShowInExplorerToolTip
data.comment: Explorer is the Windows file manager - use whatever Windows calls it in your language.

data.name: Configs_UpdatePolicyLabel
data.comment: Label to the left of a dropdown.

data.name: Configs_UpdatePolicyToolTip
data.value: Applies to every config file of this mod, and is remembered in Data\mod_configs.json.
data.comment: Data\mod_configs.json is a file name - leave it exactly as it is.

data.name: Configs_AuthoredFilesToolTip
data.value: A folder inside this mod holding files you wrote - presets, for instance. An update leaves it exactly as it is, and removing the mod keeps it.

data.name: Configs_SettingsElsewhereToolTip
data.value: A settings file this mod keeps somewhere nothing would look for one, so updates carry your changes into it.

data.name: Configs_NotAConfigToolTip
data.value: Stop treating the open file as one of this mod's configs - for data that happens to sit in a folder called config.
data.comment: The folder is literally named "config" on disk - that word is a folder name here, not a description.

data.name: Configs_RevertToolTip
data.value: Put back what's on disk, discarding your changes

data.name: Downloads_RetryFailed
data.comment: Button label - puts every failed download back on the queue.

data.name: Downloads_RetryFailedToolTip
data.value: Put every failed or cancelled download back on the queue.

data.name: Downloads_Description
data.value: Up to three mods download at once and they install one at a time, in the order you queued them - subscribe to as many as you like and check back here for progress.
data.comment: Subscribe is the button on a mod's page.

data.name: Downloads_StatQueue
data.comment: Heading on a small statistics box. Keep it short - the box is a fixed width.

data.name: Downloads_StatLeftToFetch
data.comment: Heading on a small statistics box: how many bytes are still to come. Keep it short.

data.name: Downloads_StatTimeToGo
data.comment: Heading on a small statistics box: the estimate for the whole queue. Keep it short.

data.name: Downloads_NotSizedYet
data.comment: Shown in place of an estimate before any size is known.

data.name: Downloads_Empty
data.value: Nothing queued yet - press Subscribe on a mod's page, or Update in its update dialog, to add something here.
data.comment: Subscribe and Update are buttons elsewhere in the app - translate them as they are translated there.

data.name: Downloads_AddonTag
data.comment: Marks a queued item as an addon rather than a mod.

data.name: Downloads_StatDownloaded
data.comment: Heading on a small statistics box on one download's row. Keep it short.

data.name: Downloads_StatSpeed
data.comment: Heading on a small statistics box. Keep it short.

data.name: Downloads_StatTimeLeft
data.comment: Heading on a small statistics box. Keep it short.

data.name: Downloads_CancelToolTip
data.value: Cancel this download and any dependencies it queued.

data.name: Downloads_RetryToolTip
data.value: Put this back on the end of the queue and try again. Nothing else is re-downloaded.

data.name: Common_Continue
data.comment: Confirms a dialog and carries on. Used by the mod-page and version-change windows.

data.name: AppUpdate_InstalledLabel
data.comment: Label to the left of the running version number.

data.name: AppUpdate_LatestLabel
data.comment: Label to the left of the newest published version number.

data.name: AppUpdate_UpToDate

data.name: AppUpdate_VersionGuideHeader
data.value: HOW TO READ THE VERSION NUMBER
data.comment: Upper case in English for emphasis - use whatever reads as a quiet heading in yours.

data.name: AppUpdate_PatternPatch
data.comment: A version number with the changing part spelled out. The x's stand for digits; CHANGE marks which part moves. Translate CHANGE if that reads better, and keep the three parts separated by dots.

data.name: AppUpdate_PatchNote
data.value: bug fix. Fixes to what's already there. Safe to skip.
data.comment: Follows the pattern above and a dash, as "x.x.CHANGE - bug fix. ...".

data.name: AppUpdate_MinorNote
data.value: feature update. Something new, or something works differently.

data.name: AppUpdate_MajorNote
data.value: major update. Significant changes; read the notes first.

data.name: AppUpdate_InstallNote
data.value: You'll be asked to open the mod page first. The app then downloads the release, closes itself, swaps in the new version and reopens. Your settings, install history and staged downloads are left alone.

data.name: MainWindow_LoadingCatalogNote
data.value: Fetching the full sp-mod.com catalog - this only happens once, future launches load instantly from cache.

data.name: MainWindow_ModsLoadedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a count. Keep the :N0.

data.name: InstallRole_Title
data.value: This looks like a headless machine

data.name: InstallRole_Intro
data.value: This install has a Fika headless launcher, which only appears on a setup that runs a headless client.

data.name: InstallRole_Explanation
data.value: A headless client hosts raids without anybody playing on it, so it needs the mods that decide how a raid goes - bots, items, locations - and none of the ones that draw things at a player. Knowing which this machine is lets a server's mod list arrive trimmed to what it actually needs.

data.name: InstallRole_Question
data.value: Does anyone play the game on this machine?

data.name: InstallRole_Note
data.value: You can change this later under Options, and it never affects a mod list of your own - only the ones a server hands you.
data.comment: Options is the page name, as in the sidebar.

data.name: InstallRole_OnlyHosts
data.comment: Answer to InstallRole_Question.

data.name: InstallRole_OnlyHostsToolTip
data.value: A dedicated headless box. A served list arrives without the mods only a player needs.

data.name: InstallRole_PlaysToo
data.comment: Answer to InstallRole_Question.

data.name: InstallRole_PlaysTooToolTip
data.value: This machine both hosts and gets played on, so it takes everything a served list names.

data.name: ServerMap_FetchAgainToolTip
data.value: Asks for the list again even if its revision hasn't moved - for when the copy you hold has been edited or deleted.

data.name: ReadModPage_Intro
data.value: Same as installing manually from sp-mod.com - open each mod's page below before this gets queued.

data.name: ModListAdd_Add
data.comment: Button that puts the picked mods on the list.

data.name: Footprint_SortByLabel
data.comment: Label to the left of a dropdown.

data.name: Footprint_WhatThisReadsBody
data.value: Each mod is read from the files it installs - how much of the game it patches, what it declares that the engine would call on a timer, and what it puts on disk. It describes what a mod contains, not what happens when you play: nothing here is timed or measured, and the app cannot see whether a declared component is ever created or whether a patch sits on something the game calls often. So these are counts, not a rating - this app has no way of knowing what any of it costs you, and deliberately does not grade anyone's work. Open a mod to see what was found and the limit of what each finding establishes.

data.name: ModListVersionChange_Title
data.value: Some versions are no longer published

data.name: ModListVersionChange_Intro
data.value: These mods aren't on sp-mod.com at the version this list names any more. Tick the ones you want installed at the newest version instead - anything left unticked is skipped.

data.name: DataFiles_Title
data.comment: Window title and the title bar of the data files window.

data.name: DataFiles_ListHeader
data.comment: The files inside the app's Data\ folder. Data\ is a folder name and stays exactly as it is.

data.name: DataFiles_ReloadToolTip
data.value: Discard unsaved edits and reread this file from disk

data.name: ModDisable_Note
data.value: Nothing is deleted either way - disabled mods keep their own files and configs, and move back untouched when re-enabled.

data.name: Configs_DisclaimerTitle
data.comment: Title of a warning banner on the Configs page.

data.name: Configs_DisclaimerMessage
data.value: Changing a mod's configuration can break the mod, or your game. That is not the mod author's responsibility to put right, so only change settings you understand - and say so when reporting a bug if you have edited a config. Every file is copied into Data\config-backups before it is saved.
data.comment: Data\config-backups is a folder name and stays exactly as it is.

data.name: Play_RoleNoticeTitle
data.value: Tell the app what this machine is

data.name: Play_RoleNoticeMessage
data.value: Options has a "What this machine is" card. Saying whether anybody plays here lets a mod list from a server arrive trimmed to what a headless actually needs - until then it arrives as it would for a player, which installs more than this machine has any use for.
data.comment: Options is the page name and "What this machine is" is the card heading there - translate both as they are translated in Nav_Options and Options_MachineRoleHeader.

data.name: AppUpdate_InfoMessage
data.value: This app has its own mod page on sp-mod.com, the same as everything else you install through this app. Updates are read from that listing through the public API, and the file downloaded is the one the page's own Download button serves. As with any other mod, the page is opened before anything is downloaded so that you can read the update - no processes are circumvented as required by sp-mod.com and its authors.

data.name: MainWindow_NoInstallMessage
data.value: You must set your SPT root in the settings first

data.name: Common_NoSptInstallFolder
data.value: No SPT install folder set - configure it on the Options page first.
data.comment: Said by every page that needs the install folder. Options is the page name, as in the sidebar.

data.name: ModStatus_Installed
data.comment: Tooltip on a mod's status icon.

data.name: ModStatus_NoCompatibleVersion
data.value: No version compatible with your SPT

data.name: ModStatus_Disabled
data.value: Disabled - installed, but not loaded by SPT

data.name: ModStatus_Conflict
data.value: Conflict - two mods need incompatible versions

data.name: ModListFile_TypeName
data.comment: The name beside the .tcfmodlist pattern in a file dialog's type list.

data.name: ModListFile_AllFiles
data.comment: The name beside the *.* pattern in a file dialog's type list. Windows has its own wording for this - use it.

data.name: Api_RateLimitedFormat
data.value: Rate limited by sp-mod.com - try again in {0:N0}s.
data.comment: {0} is a number of seconds. The s is the unit - shorten or expand it as your language does.

data.name: Api_ErrorFormat
data.comment: {0} is the message the site returned, which arrives in English and is not translated.

data.name: Api_NetworkErrorFormat
data.comment: {0} is the message from Windows or .NET, which arrives in the system's language.

data.name: ModListApply_FetchFailed_one
data.value: One mod couldn't be downloaded, so nothing was disabled.
data.comment: Said when exactly one download failed. See ModListApply_FetchFailedManyFormat for the other case - these two become one plural key in S5.

data.name: ModListApply_FetchFailed_other
data.value: {0} mods couldn't be downloaded, so nothing was disabled.
data.comment: {0} is two or more.

data.name: SptLaunch_ServerExeNotFoundFormat
data.value: No SPT server executable in {0} - check the install folder on the Options page.
data.comment: {0} is a folder path. One key per target rather than a shared sentence with the name of the thing dropped into it - a noun spliced into a sentence cannot be translated.

data.name: SptLaunch_ClientExeNotFoundFormat
data.value: No SPT launcher in {0} - check the install folder on the Options page.
data.comment: {0} is a folder path.

data.name: SptLaunch_HeadlessExeNotFoundFormat
data.value: No Fika headless launcher in {0} - check the install folder on the Options page.
data.comment: {0} is a folder path. Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: SptLaunch_ServerAlreadyRunning
data.value: The SPT server is already running.

data.name: SptLaunch_HeadlessAlreadyRunning
data.value: The headless launcher is already running.

data.name: SptLaunch_StartFailedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a process name, {1} the reason Windows gave, which arrives in the system's language.

data.name: SptLaunch_ServerNotRunning
data.value: The server isn't running, so there's nothing to restart - start it instead.

data.name: SptLaunch_HeadlessNotRunning
data.value: The headless launcher isn't running, so there's nothing to restart - start it instead.

data.name: SptLaunch_StopFailedFormat
data.value: Couldn't stop {0}. It may be running as another user or as administrator - closing its window by hand and then starting it again does the same job.
data.comment: {0} is a process name. Used when Windows gave no reason.

data.name: SptLaunch_StopFailedReasonFormat
data.value: Couldn't stop {0}: {1}. It may be running as another user or as administrator - closing its window by hand and then starting it again does the same job.
data.comment: {0} is a process name, {1} the reason Windows gave. The same sentence as SptLaunch_StopFailedFormat with the reason in it - keep the two consistent.

data.name: SptLaunch_ServerNotFoundHere
data.value: No SPT server executable found in this install.

data.name: SptLaunch_ClientNotFoundHere
data.value: No SPT launcher found in this install.

data.name: SptLaunch_HeadlessNotFoundHere
data.value: No Fika headless launcher found in this install.

data.name: SptLaunch_Running
data.comment: The resting line under a button when that thing is up.

data.name: SptLaunch_ClientRunning
data.value: Running - the game or its launcher is already open.

data.name: Common_ListPairFormat
data.comment: Joins the last two names in a list of things - "SPT.Server.exe and EscapeFromTarkov.exe". The names are process or file names and are not translated.

data.name: Common_ListSeparator
data.comment: Between every pair of names before the last two, which Common_ListPairFormat joins. Keep the trailing space if your language uses one.

data.name: Common_UnknownAmount
data.comment: Stands in for a byte size the app could not determine. It appears mid-sentence where a size like "4.2 MB" would otherwise be.

data.name: ModInstall_UnrecognisedArchiveFormat
data.value: {0} {1}'s archive doesn't look like a normal SPT mod package (no BepInEx/user/SPT folder found in it) - install it manually instead.
data.comment: {0} is a mod name, {1} a version. BepInEx, user and SPT are folder names and stay as they are.

data.name: ModInstall_PartlyInstalledFormat
data.value: {0} {1} was only partly installed - {2} of {3} files were placed before this failed: {4} Close SPT and its server, then install it again.
data.comment: {0} mod name, {1} version, {2} and {3} file counts, {4} the reason Windows gave (arrives in the system's language).

data.name: ModInstall_DownloadIncompleteFormat
data.value: The download stopped early - {0} of {1} arrived, so the archive was incomplete and nothing was installed. Retry it; if it keeps stopping, sp-mod.com's file server is cutting the transfer short.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are byte sizes, or the Common_UnknownAmount phrase.

data.name: ModInstall_UnsafeArchiveEntryFormat
data.value: Archive entry "{0}" would extract outside the target folder - refusing to extract it.
data.comment: {0} is a path inside the archive.

data.name: ModInstall_UnexpectedFormat
data.comment: {0} is the name of the failure, which is not translated.

data.name: ModInstall_NoDownloadLinkFormat
data.value: {0} {1} has no download link on sp-mod.com.
data.comment: {0} is a mod name, {1} a version.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseInstallFormat
data.value: Close {0} before installing a mod - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.
data.comment: {0} is one or more process names, joined by Common_ListSeparator and Common_ListPairFormat. One whole sentence per action rather than one sentence with the action dropped into it - a verb phrase spliced into a sentence cannot be translated.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseRemoveFormat
data.value: Close {0} before removing a mod - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseDisableFormat
data.value: Close {0} before disabling a mod - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseEnableFormat
data.value: Close {0} before enabling a mod - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseUndoFormat
data.value: Close {0} before undoing a change - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseApplyListFormat
data.value: Close {0} before applying a mod list - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseSortOutFormat
data.value: Close {0} before sorting out a duplicated mod - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.

data.name: ModInstall_InUseGenericFormat
data.value: Close {0} before changing your mods - files inside the SPT install are locked while it's running.

data.name: AppUpdate_TheNewVersion
data.comment: Stands in for a version number the app could not read. It appears mid-sentence where "1.15.0-beta" would otherwise be.

data.name: AppUpdate_TheAppExecutable
data.comment: Stands in for a file name the app could not read. It appears mid-sentence where "TCFModManager.exe" would otherwise be.

data.name: AppUpdate_NoDownloadFileFormat
data.value: sp-mod.com lists {0} but has no file attached to it. Open the mod page and download it manually.
data.comment: {0} is a version number, or the AppUpdate_TheNewVersion phrase.

data.name: AppUpdate_DownloadNotReadable
data.value: The downloaded file isn't a readable zip - the download may have been interrupted. Try again.

data.name: AppUpdate_ReleaseMissingExeFormat
data.value: The {0} release doesn't contain {1} where this app expects it. Download it from the mod page and copy it over by hand instead.
data.comment: {0} is a version, {1} a file name.

data.name: AppUpdate_StagedMissingExeFormat
data.value: The staged update is missing {0} - nothing was changed.
data.comment: {0} is a file name.

data.name: AppUpdate_StagedTooSmallSizedFormat
data.value: The staged {0} is only {1}KB, which is far too small to be a real build - nothing was changed.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, {1} a size in kilobytes. KB is the unit - write it as your language does.

data.name: AppUpdate_StagedTooSmallFormat
data.value: The staged {0} is far too small to be a real build - nothing was changed.
data.comment: Used when the size itself could not be read.

data.name: AppUpdate_UpdaterWouldNotStartFormat
data.value: Couldn't start the updater script. The new version is downloaded and unpacked in {0} - close the app and copy what's in there over this folder to finish by hand.
data.comment: {0} is a folder path.

data.name: AppUpdate_FolderNotWritableFormat
data.value: This app can't write to its own folder ({0}), so it can't update itself in place. Move it somewhere outside Program Files, or download the new version from the mod page and replace it by hand.
data.comment: {0} is a folder path. Program Files is a Windows folder - use whatever Windows calls it in your language.

data.name: AppUpdate_NoSpaceSizedFormat
data.value: Not enough free space on {0} to download and unpack the update - about {1}MB is needed, {2}MB is free.
data.comment: {0} is a drive name, {1} and {2} are sizes in megabytes. MB is the unit.

data.name: AppUpdate_NoSpaceFormat
data.value: Not enough free space on {0} to download and unpack the update.
data.comment: Used when the sizes could not be read.

data.name: AppUpdate_UnexpectedFormat
data.value: The update failed: {0}. Nothing was changed - download it from the mod page and replace this folder by hand if it keeps happening.
data.comment: {0} is the reason, which arrives in the system's language.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NotUpdatedNamedFormat
data.value: Your {0} couldn't be copied aside, so your version was left in place and the new one wasn't installed.
data.comment: {0} is a file name.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NotUpdatedCountFormat
data.value: {0} of your config files couldn't be copied aside, so your version was left in place and the new one wasn't installed.
data.comment: {0} is two or more.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_MergedFormat
data.value: Your settings were carried into the new defaults ({0} of them).
data.comment: {0} is how many settings were carried.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_MergedWithLostFormat
data.value: Your settings were carried into the new defaults ({0} of them); {1} could not be and are listed on the Configs page.
data.comment: {0} carried, {1} lost. Configs is the page name, as in the sidebar.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReplacedNamedFormat
data.value: Your {0} was replaced by this version's defaults.
data.comment: {0} is a file name.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReplacedOneWhereFormat
data.value: Your {0} was replaced by this version's defaults - your copy is in Data\LegacyConfigs\{1}.
data.comment: {0} is a file name, {1} a folder name. Data\LegacyConfigs\ is a path and stays as it is.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReplacedCountFormat
data.value: {0} of your config files were replaced by this version's defaults.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReplacedManyWhereFormat
data.value: {0} of your config files were replaced by this version's defaults - your copy is in Data\LegacyConfigs\{1}.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReplacedFirstTime
data.value: The app hadn't recorded what the last version shipped, so it couldn't tell your changes from the mod's.
data.comment: A second sentence, added after one of the ConfigUpdate_Replaced* ones.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_RemovedNamedFormat
data.value: Your {0} is no longer part of the mod.
data.comment: {0} is a file name.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_RemovedOneWhereFormat
data.value: Your {0} is no longer part of the mod - your copy is in Data\LegacyConfigs\{1}.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_RemovedCountFormat
data.value: {0} of your config files are no longer part of the mod.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_RemovedManyWhereFormat
data.value: {0} of your config files are no longer part of the mod - your copy is in Data\LegacyConfigs\{1}.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_VersionRangeFormat
data.comment: Two version numbers, as in "Updating to 1.2 to 1.3". Used where one version number would otherwise be.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteMerged_one
data.value: Updating to {0} kept 1 setting of yours in this file.
data.comment: {0} is a version, or a version range from ConfigUpdate_VersionRangeFormat. The one-setting case; see the Many form.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteMerged_other
data.value: Updating to {0} kept {1} settings of yours in this file.
data.comment: {1} is two or more. These two become one plural key in S5.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_AlsoDroppedFormat
data.value: It also reported {0} the update no longer has.
data.comment: {0} is a count of settings.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_AlsoAddedFormat
data.value: It also reported {0} you added yourself, which it could not place.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_AlsoBothFormat
data.value: It also reported {0} the update no longer has, and {1} you added yourself, which it could not place.
data.comment: Both counts in one sentence rather than two clauses joined by a conjunction.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteReplacedFormat
data.value: Updating to {0} replaced this file with the version's defaults.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteReplacedWhereFormat
data.value: Updating to {0} replaced this file with the version's defaults - your copy is in Data\LegacyConfigs\{1}.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReasonNoBaseline
data.value: The app had nothing to compare it against yet; the next update can carry your changes.
data.comment: A second sentence, added after one of the ConfigUpdate_NoteReplaced* ones.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReasonTakeNew
data.value: This mod is set to take the new file.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReasonNotMergeable
data.value: Its format is not one the merge can read - set this mod to keep yours if you edit it.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_ReasonTooLarge
data.value: It holds too much to be settings, so it was left as the mod shipped it.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteKeptMineFormat
data.value: Updating to {0} left this file exactly as it was, as you asked.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteDefaultsUpdatedFormat
data.value: Updating to {0} brought this file's defaults with it. Nothing of yours was in it.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NotePreservedFormat
data.value: Updating to {0} left this file exactly as it is - it is one of yours, not the mod's.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteNotUpdatedFormat
data.value: Updating to {0} could not copy this file aside, so it was left alone.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteAddedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a version number.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_NoteUnchangedFormat
data.value: Updating to {0} left this file unchanged.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_PolicyKeepMine
data.value: Your file is left exactly as it is. A setting the new version adds will be missing from it, which some mods handle and some don't.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_PolicyTakeNew
data.value: The new version's file wins. Your copy is kept in Data\LegacyConfigs so you can put values back by hand.
data.comment: Data\LegacyConfigs is a folder name and stays as it is.

data.name: ConfigUpdate_PolicyMerge
data.value: The new version's file is used, with the settings you changed carried into it. A setting the update adds arrives at its default; one it removes is reported and dropped.

data.name: ServerMap_ConnectedFormat
data.comment: {0} is the server's name, or its address when it has no name.

data.name: ServerMap_ConnectedWithVersionFormat
data.comment: {1} is an SPT version number.

data.name: ServerMap_FirstConnectionFormat
data.value: Recorded its certificate ({0}) - you'll be warned if it changes.
data.comment: A second sentence, added after one of the ServerMap_Connected* ones. {0} is a shortened fingerprint.

data.name: ServerMap_NoAddress
data.value: No server address set - enter the same address you put in the SPT launcher.

data.name: ServerMap_InvalidAddressFormat
data.value: "{0}" and port {1} don't make an address this app can dial. The port has to be a number between 1 and 65535.
data.comment: {0} is what was typed as the host, {1} as the port.

data.name: ServerMap_UnreachableFormat
data.value: Nothing answered at {0}:{1}. The server may not be running, or the address or port may be wrong - it's the same one you use in the SPT launcher.
data.comment: {0} is a host, {1} a port.

data.name: ServerMap_CertificateChangedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a host, {1} and {2} are shortened fingerprints. The line breaks and the two labels are laid out to be compared by eye - keep them on their own lines.

data.name: ServerMap_NotServerMapFormat
data.value: Something is running at {0}:{1}, but it isn't a server with the Server Map mod installed. Ask whoever runs it to add it - the map needs the mod on the server, not just this app.
data.comment: Server Map is the mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_ProtocolNewerFormat
data.value: That server's Server Map is newer than this app understands (it speaks version {0}, this app speaks {1}). Update Steamified SPT Mod Manager.
data.comment: Steamified SPT Mod Manager is this app's name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_ProtocolOlderFormat
data.value: That server's Server Map is older than this app understands (it speaks version {0}, this app speaks {1}). Ask whoever runs it to update the mod.

data.name: ServerMap_ReachFailedFormat
data.comment: {2} is the reason, which arrives in the system's language.

data.name: ServerMap_NotSetUp
data.value: Not set up. Enter a server address to connect.

data.name: ServerMap_ServingOwnList_one
data.value: This server is serving your own list "{0}" (revision {1}, 1 mod). It stays yours to edit on the Collections page - publish it again after a change to update what the server hands out.
data.comment: {0} is a list name the user typed. Mod lists is the page name, as in the sidebar. The one-mod case; see the Many form.

data.name: ServerMap_ServingOwnList_other
data.value: This server is serving your own list "{0}" (revision {1}, {2} mods). It stays yours to edit on the Collections page - publish it again after a change to update what the server hands out.
data.comment: {2} is two or more. These two become one plural key in S5.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSaved_one
data.value: "{0}" (revision {1}, 1 mod) is saved in your mod lists. Applying it is done from the Collections page, which shows what would change first.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSaved_other
data.value: "{0}" (revision {1}, {2} mods) is saved in your mod lists. Applying it is done from the Collections page, which shows what would change first.

data.name: ServerMap_NoListHeldFormat
data.value: This server isn't publishing a mod list. "{0}" is still in your mod lists as you last fetched it - though if you were expecting to see it here, check the address is the server you published it to, and that the file reached that server's config folder.
data.comment: {0} is a list name.

data.name: ServerMap_NoList
data.value: This server doesn't publish a mod list. Its operator publishes one with "Publish to this server" on the Collections page, from the app on the machine running the server.
data.comment: "Publish to this server" is the button named in ModLists_Publish - translate it the same way.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyRequired
data.value: This server needs a shared key before it will send its list. Ask whoever runs it for the key and put it in the box above - they'll find it in the mod's config folder, in servermap-key.txt.
data.comment: servermap-key.txt is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyRejected
data.value: The server didn't accept the key. Check it against the one whoever runs the server has - it may have been re-generated since they sent it to you. Dashes and capitals don't matter.

data.name: ServerMap_ListUnreadableFormat
data.value: The server sent a list this app couldn't read - {0}.
data.comment: {0} is a parse error, which is not translated.

data.name: ServerMap_ListCertificateRejected
data.value: The list wasn't fetched - the server's certificate is not the one this app recorded.

data.name: ServerMap_ListFailedReasonFormat
data.comment: {0} is the reason, which arrives in the system's language.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyNeeded
data.value: This server needs a key. Whoever runs it will find it in the Server Map mod's config folder, in servermap-key.txt.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyOptional

data.comment: Badge on a finding.

data.name: Footprint_AreaDisk
data.comment: Badge on a finding: space taken on disk.

data.name: Footprint_AreaUnknown
data.comment: Badge on a finding the app could not read, so it can say nothing about where the cost falls.

data.name: Footprint_AreaNote
data.comment: Badge on a finding that reports a limit of the reading rather than something the mod does.

data.name: Footprint_AreaNotLoaded
data.comment: Badge on the first finding of a disabled mod: its files are read but SPT is not loading them.

data.name: Footprint_TitleFormat
data.comment: {0} is a mod name, {1} its version. Both are data and are not translated; only the spacing between them is yours.

data.name: Footprint_FactSeparator
data.comment: Between the facts on a mod's collapsed line - "3 patch classes · 4.1 MB · disabled". Change the character if another reads better in your language.

data.name: Footprint_DetailPatch_one
data.comment: One fact on the collapsed line. See the Many form; these become one plural key in S5.

data.name: Footprint_DetailPatch_other
data.comment: One fact on the collapsed line.

data.name: Footprint_DetailComponent_one
data.comment: One fact on the collapsed line.

data.name: Footprint_DetailComponent_other
data.comment: One fact on the collapsed line.

data.name: Footprint_DetailDisabled
data.comment: One fact on the collapsed line, lower case because it sits among the others.

data.name: Footprint_Components_one
data.value: Declares 1 component the engine would call on a timer
data.comment: What the files contain, never what happens while playing - keep "declares" rather than "runs".

data.name: Footprint_Components_other
data.value: Declares {0} components the engine would call on a timer
data.comment: Keep "declares" rather than "runs" - see the One form.

data.name: Footprint_ComponentsEffect
data.value: This is what the mod contains, not what happens when you play: a declared component only runs if an instance of it is created, attached to an active object and enabled, and none of that is visible in the files. The lines below say which kind of callback each one uses - a component declaring more than one appears in more than one line, so those can add up to more than this total.

data.name: Footprint_FrameUpdate_one
data.value: 1 of those declares a per-frame update method

data.name: Footprint_FrameUpdate_other
data.value: {0} of those declare a per-frame update method

data.name: Footprint_FrameUpdateEffect
data.value: Unity calls Update or LateUpdate on a component once a frame while it is alive and enabled. This is the kind of work that tracks frame rate most directly - though how much it costs depends entirely on what the code inside does.
data.comment: Update, LateUpdate and Unity are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_Physics_one
data.value: 1 of those declares a physics-step method

data.name: Footprint_Physics_other
data.value: {0} of those declare a physics-step method

data.name: Footprint_PhysicsEffect
data.value: FixedUpdate runs on the physics timestep - fifty times a second by default - and not once a frame. It can run several times in one frame or not at all in another, so its cost does not track your frame rate the way an Update does.
data.comment: FixedUpdate and Update are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_Gui_one
data.value: 1 of those draws with immediate-mode GUI

data.name: Footprint_Gui_other
data.value: {0} of those draw with immediate-mode GUI

data.name: Footprint_GuiEffect
data.value: Unity calls OnGUI more than once a frame - a layout pass, then once per input event - and immediate-mode code typically allocates on each call, which adds garbage collection pressure. What it actually draws decides how much that matters.
data.comment: OnGUI and Unity are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_ImageEffect_one
data.value: 1 of those is a full-screen image effect

data.name: Footprint_ImageEffect_other
data.value: {0} of those are full-screen image effects

data.name: Footprint_ImageEffectEffect
data.value: OnRenderImage takes the rendered frame and writes a new one, for each camera the component is attached to. That work is done by the graphics card and scales with resolution rather than with processor speed.
data.comment: OnRenderImage is a name from the game engine and stays as it is.

data.name: Footprint_Camera_one
data.value: 1 of those hooks a camera's render

data.name: Footprint_Camera_other
data.value: {0} of those hook a camera's render

data.name: Footprint_CameraEffect
data.value: OnPreRender and OnPostRender run either side of a camera drawing, once per camera per frame. They run on the processor rather than the graphics card, whatever the code inside them may go on to set up.
data.comment: OnPreRender and OnPostRender are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_Patches_one
data.comment: Keep "ships" rather than "runs" - this is what the files contain.

data.name: Footprint_Patches_other
data.comment: Keep "ships" rather than "runs".

data.name: Footprint_PatchesEffect
data.value: A patch class alters one of the game's own methods - usually a single one, though one class can target several, so this is a floor rather than a total. Where a patch sits is what decides its cost, and that is exactly what reading the files cannot establish: a patch on a method the game calls thousands of times a second is indistinguishable here from one on a menu button. Read this as how far the mod reaches, not as what it costs.

data.name: Footprint_BundlesFormat
data.comment: {0} is a size, {1} a file count. .bundle is a file extension and stays as it is. Used for both the client and the server half.

data.name: Footprint_BundlesEffect
data.value: Asset bundles hold textures, models, sounds and shaders, and take up memory once loaded - video memory too, for anything the graphics card needs. These are identified by their file extension and measured on disk; when and whether the mod loads them is its own business.

data.name: Footprint_Patcher
data.comment: BepInEx is the mod loader's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Footprint_PatcherEffect
data.value: BepInEx runs patchers in its preloader, before the game's own assemblies are loaded. That is a start-up cost, and it is not running once you are in a raid.
data.comment: BepInEx is the mod loader's name and stays as it is. A raid is a match in Escape from Tarkov.

data.name: Footprint_ServerHalf
data.comment: user\mods is a folder path and stays as it is.

data.name: Footprint_ServerHalfEffect
data.value: These load in the SPT server process rather than in the game. Their cost falls on server start-up and raid loading; they are not in the client's frame loop, so they cannot cost you frame rate directly.

data.name: Footprint_ServerPatches_one
data.value: 1 of those is a patch class

data.name: Footprint_ServerPatchesEffect
data.value: Found in the server half, so this alters the server rather than the game. It is counted separately from the client figure above and does not affect this mod's level, which describes the client only.

data.name: Footprint_ServerBundlesEffect
data.value: These sit in the server half, so they are the server's memory rather than the game's.

data.name: Footprint_DiskFormat
data.comment: {0} is a size, {1} a file count.

data.name: Footprint_DiskAssembliesNone
data.value: None of them are managed assemblies, so there was no compiled code here to read.
data.comment: Followed by Footprint_DiskEffectTail, joined by Common_SentenceSeparator.

data.name: Footprint_DiskAssemblies_one
data.value: 1 of them is a managed assembly, which is what everything above was read from.
data.comment: Followed by Footprint_DiskEffectTail, joined by Common_SentenceSeparator.

data.name: Footprint_DiskAssemblies_other
data.value: {0} of them are managed assemblies, which is what everything above was read from.
data.comment: Followed by Footprint_DiskEffectTail, joined by Common_SentenceSeparator.

data.name: Footprint_DiskEffectTail
data.value: This is everything in the mod's own folders, so anything installed into them - an addon that has no folder of its own, for instance - is counted here too.
data.comment: Ends the Disk finding, after whichever assembly sentence applies.

data.name: Footprint_UnreadableFormat
data.value: {0} of {1} assemblies could not be read
data.comment: {0} is how many could not be read, {1} how many there are.

data.name: Footprint_UnreadableEffect
data.value: Every count above is a floor rather than a total. An assembly can be unreadable because it is obfuscated, packed, or built in a way this doesn't parse.

data.name: Footprint_ShowingNamesFormat
data.comment: {0} is how many names are listed, {1} how many were found.

data.name: Footprint_ShowingNamesEffect
data.value: The counts above are complete; only the list of method names below is shortened.

data.name: Footprint_ServerComponents_one
data.value: 1 type in the server half looks like a game component

data.name: Footprint_ServerComponents_other
data.value: {0} types in the server half look like game components

data.name: Footprint_ServerComponentsEffect
data.value: Server code has no reason to use them, and the check matches on type name alone, so this is more likely a coincidence of naming than real work. It is reported rather than counted as client work either way.

data.name: Footprint_NothingFound
data.value: Nothing that patches the game or runs on a timer

data.name: Footprint_NothingFoundEffect
data.value: No patch classes, and no components declaring an engine callback. Whatever this mod does, it does when something else calls it - or it is data and assets rather than code.

data.name: Footprint_NotLoadedEffect
data.value: Its files are still on disk, which is why they can still be read, but SPT is not loading any of them. Everything below describes what this mod would do once you enable it again.

data.name: Footprint_Files_one
data.comment: Used inside Footprint_BundlesFormat and Footprint_DiskFormat. See the Many form; these become one plural key in S5.

data.name: Footprint_Files_other
data.comment: Used inside Footprint_BundlesFormat and Footprint_DiskFormat.

data.name: Footprint_CallbacksFormat
data.comment: Tooltip listing the method names found. {0} is those names, joined by Common_ListSeparator; they are code identifiers and are not translated.

data.name: Footprint_CallbacksTruncatedFormat
data.comment: Same as Footprint_CallbacksFormat, for when more were found than are listed.

data.name: Footprint_StatusRereading
data.comment: Shown while Rescan re-reads every mod instead of using the cache.

data.name: Footprint_StatusNone
data.value: No installed mods found. Set your SPT install folder on the Options page.
data.comment: The Options page is named by Nav_Options - translate both the same way.

data.name: Footprint_Status_one
data.value: 1 mod read from what it ships on disk.
data.comment: See the Many form; these become one plural key in S5.

data.name: Footprint_Status_other
data.value: {0} mods read from what they ship on disk.

data.name: Browse_CountFound_other

data.name: ModUpdate_ParentNotInstalledUnnamed

data.comment: Shown in place of ModUpdate_ParentNotInstalledFormat when the parent mod's name is not known.

data.name: ModUpdate_DowngradeTitleFormat
data.comment: {0} is a mod name, {1} the version being installed. Dialog title.

data.name: ModUpdate_DowngradeBodyFormat
data.value:
You have {0} installed, and this will replace it with {1}.
Replacing the files is the easy half. What this app cannot undo is anything the newer version has already written - its own config files, and any changes it made to your SPT profile. An older build may not read those back, and some mods change their data format between versions, which can leave a profile the older version refuses to load.
Back up your profile before continuing if it matters to you.
data.comment: {0} is the installed version, {1} the older version being installed over it.

data.name: ModUpdate_ANewerVersion
data.comment: Stands in for an installed version the app could not determine. It appears mid-sentence in ModUpdate_DowngradeBodyFormat, so it is lower case in English.

data.name: ModUpdate_NotInCatalogFormat
data.value: Couldn't find {0} in the cached catalog - try Rescan.
data.comment: {0} is a mod name. Rescan is the button named by Common_Rescan - translate both the same way.

data.name: ModUpdate_HandInstalledUpdateTitleFormat
data.comment: {0} is a mod name. Dialog title.

data.name: ModUpdate_HandInstalledRedownloadTitleFormat
data.comment: {0} is a mod name. Dialog title.

data.name: ModUpdate_HandInstalledDowngradeTitleFormat
data.comment: {0} is a mod name. Dialog title.

data.name: ModUpdate_HandInstalledUpdateBody
data.value: This mod wasn't installed through this app, so there's no record of exactly which files its current version placed - updating installs the selected version's files on top of what's already there rather than cleanly removing the old version first. You may end up with leftover files from the old version.
data.comment: One whole paragraph per action rather than one with the verb dropped into it. The app used to build "updating" from the button's label by English spelling rules, which no other language follows.

data.name: ModUpdate_HandInstalledRedownloadBody
data.value: This mod wasn't installed through this app, so there's no record of exactly which files its current version placed - redownloading installs the selected version's files on top of what's already there rather than cleanly removing the old version first. You may end up with leftover files from the old version.

data.name: ModUpdate_HandInstalledDowngradeBody
data.value: This mod wasn't installed through this app, so there's no record of exactly which files its current version placed - downgrading installs the selected version's files on top of what's already there rather than cleanly removing the old version first. You may end up with leftover files from the old version.

data.name: ModUpdate_QueuedFormat
data.value: Queued {0} {1} - see the Downloads page for progress.
data.comment: {0} is a mod name, {1} its version. Downloads is the page name - translate it as in Nav_Downloads.

data.name: ModUpdate_RecordedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a mod name, {1} a version.

data.name: ModUpdate_MarkedUpToDateFormat
data.comment: {0} is a mod name, {1} the newest published version.

data.name: ModUpdate_ClearedOverrideFormat
data.value: Cleared the manual override for {0} - it'll go back to auto-detecting from the files on disk.
data.comment: {0} is a mod name.

data.name: Options_SkipGateBody
data.value:
A mod's page is where its author puts install steps, requirements, known conflicts and warnings. Some mods won't work if you skip that, and this app has no way of telling you which ones.
Turn this off and mods are downloaded and installed straight away, without showing you any of it. Knowing what a mod needs becomes yours to keep track of.
You can turn it back on at any time.
data.comment: Shown when turning off the read-the-mod-page gate. Deliberately blunt - it is the one thing standing between someone and installing a mod whose page says it needs something this app cannot see.

data.name: Options_SkipGateTitle
data.value: Stop asking me to read mod pages?
data.comment: Dialog title.

data.name: Options_WindowRememberNote
data.value: The window will reopen wherever you leave it.
data.comment: Shown under the window startup dropdown. Matches Options_WindowRemember.

data.name: Options_WindowMaximisedNote
data.comment: Matches Options_WindowMaximised.

data.name: Options_WindowCustomNote
data.value: The window will open at the size below.
data.comment: Matches Options_WindowCustom.

data.name: Options_WindowFullScreenNote
data.value: The window will open full screen. F11 leaves full screen at any time.
data.comment: Matches Options_WindowFullScreen. F11 is a keyboard key and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_WindowSizeSavedFormat
data.value: Saved - the window will open at {0} x {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the width in pixels, {1} the height. The x between them is yours to change.

data.name: Options_WindowSizeRestoreFirst
data.value: Restore the window down from maximised or full screen first - there is no chosen size to read while it fills the screen.
data.comment: Shown when Use current size is pressed while the window is maximised or full screen.

data.name: Options_BrowseNoDefault
data.value: Browse: no default saved - it opens sorted by newest, filtered to your installed SPT version.
data.comment: Browse is the page name - translate it as in Nav_Browse.

data.name: Options_BrowseHasDefault
data.value: Browse: a default is saved. Clearing it takes effect the next time the app starts.
data.comment: Browse is the page name - translate it as in Nav_Browse.

data.name: Options_HeadlessPickerTitle
data.comment: Title of the file picker. Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_HeadlessPickerFilter
data.comment: Windows file-picker filter. Translate only the two descriptions - "Programs" and "All files". Everything else is machine-read: keep every | and the patterns between them exactly as they are, in the same order.

data.name: Options_RoleHeadless
data.value: Dedicated headless. A mod list a server hands this machine arrives without the mods only a player would need - it still gets everything that decides how a raid goes.
data.comment: What this machine is, when it runs a headless client but nobody plays on it. A raid is a match in Escape from Tarkov.

data.name: Options_RolePlaysAndHosts
data.value: Plays and hosts. A served list arrives whole, because both kinds of mod have somewhere to be useful here.
data.comment: What this machine is, when it both plays and runs a headless client.

data.name: Options_RoleNeither
data.value: Neither switch is on, so this reads as an ordinary player install - the same as leaving both alone. Turn one on rather than relying on that.
data.comment: What this machine is, when both switches are off.

data.name: Options_RolePlayer
data.value: An ordinary player install. A served list arrives as it always has.
data.comment: What this machine is, when somebody plays on it and it runs no headless client.

data.name: Options_InstallPathPickerTitle
data.value: Select your SPT install folder (the one with EscapeFromTarkov.exe)
data.comment: Title of the folder picker. EscapeFromTarkov.exe is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_LocalKeyDescriptionFormat
data.value: This machine runs a Server Map server. Its key is {0} - send it to whoever should be able to see what this server publishes, along with the address and port.
data.comment: {0} is the shared key. Server Map is the mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyRotateFailed
data.value: Couldn't write a new key. Check that this machine's Server Map config folder isn't read-only.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyRotated
data.value: New key generated. Send it to anyone who connects to this server - the old one stopped working just now. The server picks it up on its own; it does not need restarting.

data.name: Options_ServerMapToolTipOn
data.value: The Server map page is in the sidebar. It only has anything to show once you point it at an SPT server whose operator has installed the Server Map mod.
data.comment: On the Server map switch. Server map is the page named by Nav_ServerMap; Server Map is the mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_ServerMapToolTipOff
data.value: Adds a page that connects to an SPT server running the Server Map mod and shows what it runs, so you can compare it against your own install. Needs the mod on the server - installing this app is not enough on its own.
data.comment: On the Server map switch, when the page is off.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSummary_one
data.comment: A held mod list in one line. {0} is the list's name, {1} its revision number. See the Many form; these become one plural key in S5.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSummary_other
data.comment: {0} is the list's name, {1} its revision number, {2} how many mods it names.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSummaryOneUnresolvedFormat
data.value: {0} - revision {1}, 1 mod, {2} not on The Forge
data.comment: {2} is how many of the list's entries have no sp-mod.com listing. The Forge is sp-mod.com's own name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSummaryManyUnresolvedFormat
data.value: {0} - revision {1}, {2} mods, {3} not on The Forge
data.comment: {3} is how many of the list's entries have no sp-mod.com listing.

data.name: ServerMap_EndpointFormat
data.comment: A server's address. {0} is a host name, {1} a port number - both are data. Only the separator between them is yours, and most languages keep the colon.

data.name: ServerMap_DetailSptFormat
data.comment: One fact on the server's detail line. {0} is an SPT version number. SPT is the platform's name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_DetailModFormat
data.comment: One fact on the server's detail line. {0} is the mod's version number. Server Map is the mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_DetailPublishingFormat
data.comment: One fact on the server's detail line, so it is lower case in English. {0} is a revision number, or Common_Unknown when the server did not say.

data.name: ServerMap_DetailNoList
data.comment: One fact on the server's detail line, so it is lower case in English.

data.name: ServerMap_DetailSeparator
data.comment: Between the facts on the server's detail line. Change the character if another reads better in your language.

data.name: ModPageGate_SkipNotice
data.value: You are skipping this mod's page, and its release notes with it - it is recommended you read them first. They are where the author says what changed, what a version needs and what it breaks.
data.comment: Added under an install button's tooltip while the read-the-mod-page gate is off.

data.name: ModPageGate_Install
data.comment: Tooltip on the Install button.

data.name: ModPageGate_Redownload
data.comment: Tooltip on the Redownload button.

data.name: ModPageGate_Update
data.comment: Tooltip on the Update button.

data.name: Options_ModPagesToolTipSkipping
data.value: You are skipping each mod's release notes. It is recommended you read them - they are where an author says what changed, what a version needs and what it breaks. This app's own updates always ask regardless.
data.comment: On the read-the-mod-page switch, when the gate is off.

data.name: Options_ModPagesToolTipAsking
data.value: Each mod's page opens before anything downloads, so its release notes and install instructions are in front of you first.
data.comment: On the read-the-mod-page switch, when the gate is on.

data.name: Options_FootprintToolTipOn
data.value: The Mod footprint page is in the sidebar. Remember that it reads files rather than timing anything - what a mod actually costs depends on your hardware, your settings and the other mods you run, none of which it can see.
data.comment: On the Mod footprint switch. Mod footprint is the page named by Nav_Footprint.

data.name: Options_FootprintToolTipOff
data.value: Adds a page that reads what each installed mod ships and describes how much of the game it is positioned to touch. Nothing on it is timed or measured, and a heavy footprint is not the same as a mod that costs you frames.
data.comment: On the Mod footprint switch, when the page is off.
