data.name: AppUpdate_ChangePatch
data.comment: The kind of update, from how the version number changed.

data.name: AppUpdate_ChangeMinor
data.comment: The kind of update, from how the version number changed.

data.name: AppUpdate_ChangeMajor
data.comment: The kind of update, from how the version number changed.

data.name: AppUpdate_ChangeUnknown
data.comment: Shown when the version numbers cannot be compared.

data.name: AppUpdate_PatchBodyFormat
data.value: {0} only changes the last number (x.x.●), so it's fixes to how the current version already works - nothing new to learn. Safe to skip if nothing is broken for you.
data.comment: {0} is the new version number. The x.x.● picture shows which part of the number changed - keep it as it is.

data.name: AppUpdate_MinorBodyFormat
data.value: {0} changes the middle number (x.●.x), so it adds features or changes how something works. Worth reading the notes below before updating.
data.comment: {0} is the new version number.

data.name: AppUpdate_MajorBodyFormat
data.value: {0} changes the first number (●.x.x), so this is a major update - expect significant changes. Read the notes below and the mod page before updating.
data.comment: {0} is the new version number.

data.name: AppUpdate_UnknownBodyFormat
data.value: sp-mod.com lists {0}, but it isn't numbered in a way this app can compare against {1}. Check the mod page to see what changed.
data.comment: {0} is the published version, {1} the one installed.

data.name: AppUpdate_BannerTitleFormat
data.comment: {0} is one of the AppUpdate_Change keys, {1} the new version number.

data.name: AppUpdate_DownloadSizeFormat
data.comment: How big the update is. MB is the international symbol and normally stays as it is. Keep the :N0.

data.name: AppUpdate_PublishedFormat
data.comment: When the update was published. Replace d MMMM yyyy with the date pattern your language uses - d is the day, MMMM the month's name, yyyy the year.

data.name: AppUpdate_RateLimited
data.value: sp-mod.com is rate limiting right now. Try again in a minute.

data.name: AppUpdate_UnreachableFormat
data.comment: {0} is the underlying network error, which arrives in English.

data.name: AppUpdate_TimedOut
data.value: Timed out reaching sp-mod.com - check your connection and try again.

data.name: AppUpdate_CheckUnexpectedFormat
data.comment: {0} is the underlying error, which arrives in English.

data.name: AppUpdate_DownloadingFormat
data.comment: {0} is the new version number.

data.name: AppUpdate_DownloadingProgressFormat
data.comment: {0} is the new version number, {1} how far through. Keep the :P0 - it writes the percent sign the way your language does.

data.name: AppUpdate_Restarting
data.value: Closing and restarting to finish the update...

data.name: PreLaunch_NoAnswerNoListFormat

data.comment: {0} is the address that was tried.

data.name: PreLaunch_NoAnswerHeldListFormat
data.value: {0} didn't answer, so this is checked against "{1}" as it was last fetched. Launching is unaffected.

data.name: PreLaunch_ListMovedFormat
data.value: The server is publishing revision {0} of "{1}"; you have revision {2}. Fetch it on the Server map page and review what changed before you join.
data.comment: {0} is the server's revision number, {1} the list's name, {2} the revision held. Server map is the page named by Nav_ServerMap.

data.name: PreLaunch_NotFetchedFormat
data.value: {0} publishes a mod list you haven't fetched yet. Get it on the Server map page to see how your install compares.
data.comment: {0} is the server's name.

data.name: PreLaunch_NoListFormat
data.value: Connected to {0}, which doesn't publish a mod list - so there's nothing to check your install against.
data.comment: {0} is the server's name.

data.value: Your install matches "{0}" (revision {1}) - the 1 mod the server expects is present and at the right version.

data.name: PreLaunch_Matches_other
data.value: Your install matches "{0}" (revision {1}) - {2} mods the server expects, all present and at the right versions.
data.comment: {0} is the list's name, {1} its revision number, {2} how many mods it names.

data.name: PreLaunch_BehindCount_one
data.value: 1 mod to install, update or enable
data.comment: One part of the outstanding-work sentence. See the Many form; these become one plural key in S5.

data.name: PreLaunch_BehindCount_other
data.value: {0} mods to install, update or enable
data.comment: One part of the outstanding-work sentence.

data.name: PreLaunch_Manual_one
data.comment: One part of the outstanding-work sentence.

data.name: PreLaunch_Manual_other

Two labelled counts rather than a sentence: a sentence with two counts in it needs a plural form for every combination the two can make - four in English, sixteen in Czech, thirty-six in Arabic - and none of that survives translation intact. {0} is how many config files, {1} how many mods they belong to. data.value: Choose whether this app installs mods for you, or only downloads them so you can install them yourself. Browsing, update checks and dependencies keep working either way. Whichever you pick, every install button has a small button beside it that does the other one, for that mod alone.

data.name: Options_UpdateNotificationsDescription
data.value: While the app is open, it asks The Forge every so often about the mods you have installed, and shows a Windows notification when one of them has a new release. data.name: Help_Start_Setup_Title

data.name: Help_Start_Setup_Step1
data.value: Open {0} - the gear at the top right.
data.comment: Each {n} is the label of a control, filled in by the app and shown in bold - keep every placeholder, move it wherever the sentence needs it.

data.name: Help_Start_Setup_Step2
data.value: Under {0}, press {1} and pick your SPT game folder - the one with EscapeFromTarkov.exe in it, not the server folder inside it.
data.comment: Each {n} is the label of a control, filled in by the app and shown in bold - keep every placeholder, move it wherever the sentence needs it.

data.name: Help_Start_Setup_Step3
data.value: Press {0}. The line underneath should now name your SPT version.
data.comment: Each {n} is the label of a control, filled in by the app and shown in bold - keep every placeholder, move it wherever the sentence needs it.

data.name: Help_Start_Setup_Note
data.value: The app isn't a mod. Keep it in a folder of its own, never in BepInEx\plugins or user\mods.
data.comment: Folder names are literal - don't translate them.

data.name: Help_Start_Version_Title

data.name: Help_Start_Version_Step2
data.value: If it's missing or wrong, open {0} and read the line under {1}.
data.comment: Each {n} is the label of a control, filled in by the app and shown in bold - keep every placeholder, move it wherever the sentence needs it.

data.name: Help_Start_Version_Step3
data.value: A version that can't be found usually means the folder is one level too deep. Pick the folder with EscapeFromTarkov.exe in it and press {0}.
data.comment: Each {n} is the label of a control, filled in by the app and shown in bold - keep every placeholder, move it wherever the sentence needs it.

data.name: Help_Browse_Compatible_Step2
data.value: Hover a card: a tick beside SPT in the box that opens means its newest version runs on yours; a cross means it doesn't.

data.name: Options_DirectLaunchSummary
data.value: Play on the Play page starts the server and the game itself - no SPT launcher window.

data.name: Options_DirectLaunchDescription
data.value: Play does what the SPT launcher does when you press its Start: starts the server if it isn't running and waits for it, checks the server and spt-core.dll are the same SPT version, cleans up the same files, applies SPT's game patch, fetches any missing mod bundles, and starts the game with the profile you picked. Profiles can be made, wiped and deleted from the Play card's ... menu. The SPT launcher's own settings (files it leaves alone, Clear cache on launch) are followed. The last game session's logs are kept for Diagnose logs.
data.comment: Options card, behind the ?.

data.name: Options_DirectLaunchWarningTitle
data.comment: Title of the warning on the Options card.

data.name: Options_DirectLaunchWarning
data.value: This copies what SPT 4.1's launcher does, read from its source code - it is not made or supported by the SPT team. A future SPT update can change how the game has to be started; SSPTMM then goes back to opening the SPT launcher for versions it doesn't know. If the game won't start or acts strangely, switch this off and use the SPT launcher, and say it was started from SSPTMM when asking for help. For everything to run in the background, also turn on starting the server without its window, above.
data.comment: Warning on the Options card.

data.value: This install is SPT {0}: Play starts the game from here.
data.comment: {0} is the SPT version.

data.name: Options_DirectLaunchUntestedFormat
data.value: This install is SPT {0}, newer than the {1} this was checked against. Play still starts the game from here, but if it fails, use the SPT launcher.
data.comment: {0} is the install's SPT version, {1} the newest version checked.

data.name: Options_DirectLaunchUnsupportedFormat
data.value: This install is SPT {0}: only SPT 4.1.3 and later in 4.1 can be started from here, so Play opens the SPT launcher.
data.comment: {0} is the SPT version.
